removability.rationale: Abilities is mostly self-contained (route + file + section), and no nav edits are needed, but the feature's tentacles reach into the Pokémon page, the API client, the models and the Node server, so full removal without dead code is a handful of small, findable edits rather than a single delete.

changeability.rationale: Most fixes land in one obvious place (sprite rule, missing-value rule, humanization), but a couple of genuine two-place edits exist: card data is constructed in two sites, and the error heading shown by LoadState is mirrored as strings in page-title.ts.

evidence: app/src/app/core/poke-api.ts:53-90 — pages depend on a narrow, well-named service interface (species/pokemon/move/type/cardsFor)
app/src/app/shared/pokemon-card-list.ts:42 — a presentational shared component injects PokeApi for spriteUrl, coupling the card UI to the data layer

coupling.rationale: Loosely coupled overall: no shared mutable state, URL is the state container, server and client code are cleanly separated files. The deductions are a presentational component reaching into the API layer, a shared→pages import, and route patterns maintained in two places.

evidence: app/src/app/core/poke-api.ts:104-115 — cardsFor with an `extra` callback absorbs the real variation (hidden-ability flag, card types) without flag parameters
app/src/app/pages/pokemon/moves-table.ts:81-100 — MovesTable is generic over columns/direction; sorting added for one table works for all
app/src/app/shared/type-badge.ts:15-18 — one small boolean (static) captures the only real variation, not flag creep
app/src/app/pages/move-page.ts:62-67 — resource + syncPageTitle + errorHeading + LoadState scaffold is copy-pasted in move/ability/type/pokemon pages

abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions sit exactly where the app's real variation is (cards, badges, move tables), so extending rarely requires copying core logic — only the ~40-line page scaffold. A small page/section helper would remove the remaining copy-paste, but nothing is over-generalized or boolean-flag-ridden.

findings.issue: The Node server hard-codes route knowledge (DETAIL_ROUTES, STATIC_ROUTES) parallel to app/src/app/app.routes.ts; adding or removing a page requires editing both and they can silently drift.
findings.suggestion: Derive the server's route patterns from a single shared list (e.g., a small module both the server and the routes file import), or generate it from the Angular routes at build time.

findings.issue: errorHeading duplicates the 'Not found' / 'Something went wrong' heading strings that LoadState renders (app/src/app/shared/load-state.ts:11-13); a wording change must be made twice.
findings.suggestion: Export the headings as constants from one module and have both LoadState and errorHeading use them, or let LoadState own the title side-effect.

findings.issue: A presentational shared component injects the API client (PokeApi) just for spriteUrl, coupling card rendering to the data layer and making the component harder to reuse or test in isolation.
findings.suggestion: Put the sprite URL (or pokemon/species name it derives from) into CardData at construction time, or make spriteUrl a pure function of the injected base URL exposed without the full service.

findings.issue: The shared/ layer imports NotFound from pages/, inverting the folder layering the app otherwise follows (core ← shared ← pages).
findings.suggestion: Move NotFound into shared/ (or core/) so the dependency points the right way.

findings.issue: CardData is constructed in two places (Home's computed and PokeApi.cardsFor at app/src/app/core/poke-api.ts:104-115), so enriching cards — e.g., using each Pokémon's real front_default sprite — requires touching both data paths.
findings.suggestion: Route Home's cards through the same construction helper (or move CardData building into one function both call), so card fields have a single origin.

findings.issue: The resource + syncPageTitle + LoadState page scaffold is copy-pasted across four detail pages, so a new section (e.g., Items) starts from a duplicated template.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small helper (e.g., a detailPageResource factory or a wrapper component owning the title/loading/not-found shell) that each page calls with its loader.

findings.issue: The resource loaders never pass Angular's abortSignal to fetch, so navigating away from a page doesn't cancel in-flight requests (they're only dropped from cache on rejection).
findings.suggestion: Thread the resource loader's abortSignal into fetch(), and consider caching resolved values rather than the promise so aborted attempts don't linger.

findings.issue: The default API origin 'http://localhost:9000' is duplicated in api-config.ts, server/server.mjs:20 and README.md, so changing the default means updating several literals.
findings.suggestion: Keep the client default only as a dev fallback and document the server as the single source (or share one constants file between server and client).

summary: This is an easy codebase to change: one data seam (PokeApi), one card renderer, pure tested helpers, modern Angular 22 idioms, and a README that documents the structure. Most edits land in one obvious place; the real frictions are the duplicated route knowledge in the Node server, a couple of mirrored constants (error headings, API origin default), and a page scaffold that gets copy-pasted per route. Every scenario I walked through was a 4–5 on difficulty.
